init.title: HomeDarts options
init.description: **Online matches (experimental):** the integration sees the darts on your board, but not the game of an online match on play.autodarts.io. The browser extension Tools for Autodarts can send its moments, such as a bust, a game shot or a 180, to Home Assistant. They arrive as board events whose type starts with `online_`.

data.online_bridge: Receive online matches from Tools for Autodarts
data.online_bridge_remote: Accept calls from outside your home network

data_description.online_bridge: Opens a secret webhook address for the browser extension. The next step shows it.
data_description.online_bridge_remote: Only for an https address through Home Assistant Cloud or your own domain. Off: only devices in your home network can call the address.
data_description.online_bridge_new_address: The current address stops working. Enter the new one in Tools for Autodarts.
data_description.plans: A list in YAML: every plan with a `name`, its `steps` and, if you like, the `weekdays` on which it is the plan of the day. The page Training plans of the documentation has an example. An empty list is none.

online_bridge.title: Address for Tools for Autodarts
online_bridge.description:
After you submit, Home Assistant accepts moments of online matches at this secret address:

`{url}`

In Tools for Autodarts, turn on **WLED**, choose **Import CSV** and paste the lines below. Each line creates an effect of type URL that calls the address with `?event=` and its trigger. Import only the lines you need: Tools for Autodarts plays one effect per trigger and picks one at random when several share a trigger.

```
{effects}
```

The *Online bridge last event* sensor shows the last moment that arrived. Keep the address to yourself: whoever knows it can send moments of a game to your Home Assistant.

wrong_board.title: Autodarts board address points to a different board
wrong_board.description: The board at {address} has a different board ID than the one this entry belongs to, so it stays offline. Open HomeDarts for Autodarts, choose **Reconfigure** and select the correct board.

board_manager_1.title: Update the board to the new Autodarts Board Manager
board_manager_1.description: This board runs the classic Board Manager app. Autodarts replaces it with the headless Board Manager 2 and will turn the old one off once most players have migrated. Install Board Manager 2 on the board PC; the integration switches over automatically and keeps working locally.

confirm.title: Calibrate now
confirm.description:
The board corrected {rate} % of the last darts. A fresh calibration usually brings this down.

Remove all darts from the board first. The calibration takes a few seconds.

abort.calibration_failed: The board did not accept the calibration. Try again, or calibrate from the board status card.
abort.board_unavailable: The board is not loaded. Check the connection and try again.

stuck_hand.title: Autodarts board sees a hand all the time

confirm.title: Restart the detection
confirm.description:
For over a minute the board has reported a hand in front of it that does not move, and it detects no darts while it does. The likely cause is light that changed while the detection ran, such as a light ring that was switched on. A calibration does not clear this; stopping and starting the detection does.

Restart the detection now? Take your hand away from the board first.

To keep this from coming back, switch the light before the detection starts, or restart the detection after switching it.

abort.restart_failed: The board did not accept the restart. Try again, or stop and start the detection with its switch.
abort.board_unavailable: The board is not loaded. Check the connection and try again.

board_access_denied.title: Autodarts board refuses access
board_access_denied.description: The board at {address} answers with HTTP 401 or 403. Board Manager itself needs no login, so something between Home Assistant and the board blocks the requests, for example a reverse proxy, a firewall or a login in front of port 3180. Let Home Assistant reach the board; the notice disappears by itself.

unsupported_response.title: Autodarts board answers in an unknown format
unsupported_response.description: The board answers {reads} in a format this version of the integration does not understand, for example after a Board Manager update. Values from these reads are not updated. Update the Autodarts integration; if the notice stays, report it together with the diagnostics.

board_moved.title: Autodarts board found at a new address

confirm.title: Use the new address
confirm.description:
A board with the board ID of this entry answers at {new}, while it no longer answers at its configured address.

Connect the board there? Confirm only if this is your board: any device on your network can claim a board ID. The integration reloads; entities, training and settings are kept.

abort.board_unavailable: The board no longer answers at the new address. Wait for the next notice, or open the integration and choose **Reconfigure**.

confirm.title: Replace the blueprint
confirm.description:
The file `{path}` matches no version of this blueprint that HomeDarts knows: you changed it, or imported it from a newer state of the repository. So the update of the integration left it as it is, while the integration brings the version of {name} that belongs to it.

Replace your file with that version? Your changes to the file are lost; the automations made from the blueprint keep their settings and reload. To keep your file, ignore this notice.

abort.not_shipped: This version of the integration no longer brings this blueprint, so your file stays as it is.
abort.write_failed: Home Assistant could not write the file. Check that the blueprints folder of your configuration can be written to, and try again.

confirm.title: Restore the backup
confirm.description:
{board} was added with nothing stored yet, and there is a backup of a board with the same board ID from {date}, such as the one written when the board was deleted.

Restore it? The board reloads with the training, the games, the player profiles with their progress and badges, the personal bests and the calendar of the backup; what it stored since it was added is replaced. If it stored player data since, that is backed up first. To start anew, ignore this notice.

abort.board_unavailable: The board is no longer set up.
abort.restore_failed: The backup could not be restored. The action homedarts.restore restores it and says why it fails.

takeover_references.title: Some automations, scripts or dashboards still use the old name

takeover_restart.title: Restart Home Assistant to finish the switch to HomeDarts

confirm.title: Restart Home Assistant
confirm.description: HomeDarts for Autodarts took over your boards and removed the files of the integration under its old name. A restart unloads it. Restart Home Assistant now?

start_game.name: Start game
start_game.description: Starts a practice game on the board: X01, Cricket, a party game or a training game, optionally with players and match format.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

game.name: Game
game.description: X01 from 101 to 1001 points, a Cricket game, a party game or a training game. A name as the game list shows it, in any language of the integration, works too, such as "Around the Clock".

players.name: Players
players.description: Names of one to four players, in throwing order. Without names, the number of players stays as it is.

legs.name: Legs per set
legs.description: Legs that win a set in a match.

in_mode.name: In mode
in_mode.description: How X01 legs start: with any dart (straight), with a double or the bullseye (double), or with a double, a treble or the bullseye (master).

out_mode.name: Out mode
out_mode.description: How X01 legs finish: on any dart (straight), on a double or the bullseye (double), or on a double, a treble or the bullseye (master).

bull_mode.name: Bull mode
bull_mode.description: What the bull scores in X01: 25 for the outer bull and 50 for the bullseye (25/50), or 50 for both (50/50). Only the bullseye counts as a double.

max_rounds.name: Max rounds
max_rounds.description: Rounds after which the lowest score wins an X01 leg, 1 to 50; a tie plays on round by round. 0 plays without a limit.

double_out.name: Double out
double_out.description: Replaced by the out mode: on is double, off is straight. X01 legs finish on a double or the bullseye.

double_in.name: Double in
double_in.description: Replaced by the in mode: on is double, off is straight. X01 legs start with a double or the bullseye.

bull_off.name: Bull-off
bull_off.description: Players throw at the bull first; the closest starts the match.

bull_off_distance.name: Bull-off by distance
bull_off_distance.description: Two darts in the same bull bed are decided by the distance the board measured instead of a rethrow.

teams.name: Teams
teams.description: Four players of X01 or a Cricket game play as two teams: players 1 and 3 against players 2 and 4.

three_in_a_bed.name: Three in a bed
three_in_a_bed.description: Wild Mouse: three darts of a visit in the same bed close a target of their own, as the rules have it. Off leaves it out.

start_scores.name: Start scores
start_scores.description: X01 start scores of the players in throwing order, for a handicap, for example 501 and 301; the bot's seat after the players has one, too. 0 or a missing score plays the game's start score. Teams play from the start scores of players 1 and 2.

holes.name: Golf holes
holes.description: Holes of a round of Golf: 9 or 18.

halve_on_miss.name: Bermuda halving
halve_on_miss.description: Bermuda: a visit without a hit halves the score, as on play.autodarts.io. Off keeps the score.

order.name: Round the World order
order.description: The order of the numbers in Round the World before the bull: 1 to 20, 20 to 1 or random.

target_score.name: Gotcha target score
target_score.description: The score Gotcha counts up to, 101 to 1001; the out mode decides how it ends.

bot_level.name: Bot level
bot_level.description: Play against the bot in X01 and the Cricket games: the 3-dart average it plays, 20 to 120; 0 plays without the bot. The bot takes the seat after the players.

start_plan.name: Start training plan
start_plan.description: Starts a training plan on the board: several training games in a row. Name a plan, give its steps, or give neither for the plan of the day.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

plan.name: Plan
plan.description: A plan that comes with the integration, or the name of a plan of your own from the options of the board.

name.name: Name
name.description: The name of a plan given by its steps, or of the plan to start.

steps.name: Steps
steps.description: The steps in order, in place of a plan. Each names a training game as `drill` and, if you like, the `darts` or `rounds` it may take, or `until: finished`, the default. With `options`, such as `low: 40` and `high: 100`, the checkout training stays among these finishes.

player.name: Player
player.description: Who trains. Without a name, player 1 stays.

next_plan_step.name: Skip training plan step
next_plan_step.description: Leaves the current step of the training plan for the next one. After the last step, the plan is finished.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

stop_plan.name: Stop training plan
stop_plan.description: Stops the training plan and its game on the board.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

delete_player.name: Delete player profile
delete_player.description: Forgets a player's statistics, personal bests and head-to-head records. The name also disappears from the personal bests of the board and the practice player names; the match history keeps it. A player of the tournament being played can be deleted once the tournament is stopped. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

name.name: Name
name.description: The player name, in any upper and lower case.

export.name: Export training data
export.description: Writes training sessions, practice matches or player profiles as a CSV or JSON file, by default to homedarts/exports in the media folder, and returns its path and a download link. Exports contain player names. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

format.name: Format
format.description: CSV for spreadsheets, or JSON. CSV with everything is a ZIP file with one CSV file per table.

what.name: Content
what.description: Training sessions and practice matches of the last 365 days, the player profiles, or everything.

folder.name: Folder
folder.description: Optional. A folder relative to the configuration folder, or an absolute path, where Home Assistant allows writing: www, a media folder or a folder listed in allowlist_external_dirs. Files in www are available at /local/ without a login. Without a folder: homedarts/exports in the media folder.

backup.name: Back up a board
backup.description: Writes everything the board stores, with the training, the games, the player profiles, their progress and badges, the personal bests, the weekly report and the calendar, to a backup file in homedarts/backups in the media folder, and returns its path and a download link. The newest five backups of every board stay. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

restore.name: Restore a backup
restore.description: Brings back a backup of homedarts.backup, or the one written when a board was deleted. The board reloads for it. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board that gets the backup. Only needed with more than one board.

file.name: Backup file
file.description: The backup, relative to the configuration folder or as an absolute path, such as /media/homedarts/backups/…, in a folder where Home Assistant allows reading: www, a media folder or a folder listed in allowlist_external_dirs.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Replace: the board stores what the backup holds, and what it stored before is gone. Merge: the profiles, progress, badges and matches of the players of a backup of another board, the sessions and matches of its calendar and its better personal bests are added to this board; a backup merged once changes nothing the second time. The players of a board merge once per source board: a backup of this board, or a second backup of a board merged before, is refused. Before either, what the board holds is backed up, so a restore can be undone.

save_highlight.name: Save highlight photo
save_highlight.description: Saves the picture of a camera as a photo named by the moment, the player and what it shows, by default in the highlight gallery, homedarts/highlights in the media folder, and returns the file and its address. It fails, and so returns nothing, when the camera is disabled or unavailable or gives no picture, or when the folder is not allowed. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: The camera that takes the photo, for example a board camera. The cameras of a board are disabled until you enable them.

folder.name: Folder
folder.description: Optional. A folder relative to the configuration folder, or an absolute path, where Home Assistant allows writing: www, a media folder or a folder listed in allowlist_external_dirs. Without a folder: the highlight gallery, homedarts/highlights in the media folder.

player.name: Player
player.description: Optional. The player in the photo, for its name and its title in the gallery.

label.name: Label
label.description: Optional. What the photo shows, at the end of its name, such as 180 or checkout-121. The gallery shows a number as the score.

clip_camera.name: Clip camera
clip_camera.description: Optional. A camera with a video stream that also records the moment as a clip beside the photo, under its name with .mp4, where the gallery plays it. The recording runs in the background, so the answer names the clip and its address at once; the file is written when the recording ends. A camera without a stream, or one that records already, leaves the photo without a clip.

clip_lookback.name: Seconds before
clip_lookback.description: Optional. How much of the clip comes before the photo, from what the running stream of the camera keeps. Default 5.

clip_duration.name: Seconds after
clip_duration.description: Optional. How much of the clip follows the photo. Default 8.

voice_sound.name: Voice pack sound
voice_sound.description: Finds the sound of a call in a voice pack of homedarts/voices in the media folder, for a media player: the first of the keys the pack has, such as 180, busted or yr_40, and one of its files at random. The answer is empty when the pack has none of them, so that the call can be spoken instead. The caller blueprints use it.

pack.name: Voice pack
pack.description: The folder of the pack in homedarts/voices of the media folder, for example russ-bray.

keys.name: Keys
keys.description: The keys of the sound; the first one the pack has counts, for example yr_40 and you_require. They are the file names of darts-caller's voice packs: 0 to 180, busted, gameshot, matchshot, yr_2 to yr_170, s1 to t20, bull, bullseye, outside or the name of a player.

generate_voice_pack.name: Generate voice pack
generate_voice_pack.description: Records a voice pack for the caller with a text-to-speech engine, such as Piper for a voice that stays at home: every score from 0 to 180, no score, the game shot and the match, what a player requires and every dart, under the file names of darts-caller's voice packs in homedarts/voices of the media folder. It takes a few minutes, one pack at a time, and replaces a pack it generated before, never one you copied there. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

tts_entity.name: Text-to-speech engine
tts_entity.description: The engine that speaks, for example Piper or Home Assistant Cloud.

language.name: Language
language.description: The language of the voice, for example en-GB or de-DE. The calls are in its language, in English for a language the integration does not speak.

pack.name: Voice pack
pack.description: The name of the pack, a folder of homedarts/voices in the media folder, for example piper-en.

voice.name: Voice
voice.description: Optional. A voice of the engine, for example en_GB-alan-medium for Piper. Without one, the engine's own.

link_player.name: Link player to person
link_player.description: Makes a player a person of Home Assistant: the person's picture appears on the scoreboard, the players card and the new game screen, which also lists players at home first. A person is one player; linking them again moves the link. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

player.name: Player
player.description: The player name, in any upper and lower case. A player without a profile gets one.

person.name: Person
person.description: The person of Home Assistant who is this player.

unlink_player.name: Unlink player
unlink_player.description: Forgets which person a player is. The player's statistics stay. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

player.name: Player
player.description: The player name, in any upper and lower case.

rename_player.name: Rename player
rename_player.description: Gives a player profile a new name and keeps everything that goes with it: statistics, badges, records, the match history, head-to-head records, the calendar and the link to a person. A name that another profile has already merges the two profiles into one, as if one player had thrown every dart. A player of the tournament being played keeps the name. For administrators; automations can use it, too.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: Only needed with more than one board.

player.name: Player
player.description: The player name, in any upper and lower case.

new_name.name: New name
new_name.description: The new name, at most 20 characters. A new spelling of the same name, such as Sam for sam, works too; the name of another profile merges the two.

start_tournament.name: Start tournament
start_tournament.description: Draws a tournament of three to 32 players and starts its first match: a round robin, a knockout, a double elimination or groups with a knockout, of X01 or Cricket matches. A tournament being played has to be stopped first.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

boards.name: Boards
boards.description: More boards that play matches of the tournament at the same time, by their device or entry: every board plays a match of its own, and the board of the action holds the tournament. Up to eight boards.

players.name: Players
players.description: Names of the players in the order of the draw: three to eight for a round robin, six or more for groups, up to 32 in every format but the round robin. Without names, the players of Tournament players play.

start_scores.name: Start scores
start_scores.description: X01 start scores of the players in the order of the names, for a handicap, for example 501, 501 and 301. 0 or a missing score plays the game's start score.

format.name: Format
format.description: Round robin: everyone plays everyone once. Knockout: the winners go on until the final. Double elimination: a player is out after the second lost match. Groups and knockout: everyone plays everyone in their group, and the best of every group go on into a knockout.

game.name: Game
game.description: X01 from 101 to 1001 points, Cricket, Cut-Throat Cricket or Tactics.

legs.name: Legs per set
legs.description: Legs that win a set in every match. Without it, the legs per set of the practice game apply.

sets.name: Sets to win
sets.description: Sets that win a match. Without it, the sets of the practice game apply.

double_out.name: Double out
double_out.description: X01 legs finish on a double or the bullseye.

double_in.name: Double in
double_in.description: X01 legs start with a double or the bullseye.

bull_off.name: Bull-off
bull_off.description: A bull-off decides who starts every match.

bull_off_distance.name: Bull-off by distance
bull_off_distance.description: Two darts in the same bull bed are decided by the distance the board measured instead of a rethrow.

third_place.name: Third-place match
third_place.description: In a knockout of four players or more, also after the groups, the losing semi-finalists play for third place.

groups.name: Groups
groups.description: Groups and knockout: the number of groups, from 2 to 8, of three to eight players each; 0 makes groups of about four players. Without it, Tournament groups applies.

advance.name: Qualifiers per group
advance.description: Groups and knockout: how many players of every group go on into the knockout, from 1 to 4 and fewer than the group has. Without it, Tournament qualifiers per group applies.

random_draw.name: Random draw
random_draw.description: Draws the order of the players at random instead of taking the order of the names.

seed.name: Seed
seed.description: A number for a random draw: the same number draws the same order.

pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Seconds between two matches, after the summary; 0 waits for Next tournament match.

summary.name: Summary
summary.description: Seconds the summary of a match shows before the pause begins.

stop_tournament.name: Stop tournament
stop_tournament.description: Ends the tournament. The match being played goes on as a practice match.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

next_tournament_match.name: Next tournament match
next_tournament_match.description: Starts the next match of the tournament without waiting for the pause to end.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

correct_dart.name: Correct dart
correct_dart.description: Puts a dart of the current visit into another bed for the practice game and the training session, as if the board had detected it there. The board keeps its own reading. The board's position of the dart is left behind: with x and y, the dart is where they say, otherwise it has no position and stays out of the dart positions.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

dart.name: Dart
dart.description: The dart of the current visit: 1, 2 or 3.

segment.name: Bed
segment.description: Where the dart is: S1 to S20, D1 to D20, T1 to T20, 25 (or S25, SB, OB) for the outer bull, BULL (or D25, DB, 50) for the bullseye, or MISS. Needed without x and y; with them, it must be the bed at that position.

x.name: Position x
x.description: Where the dart is, from left to right: 0 is the center, 1 the outer edge of the double ring. Together with y, it gives the bed.

y.name: Position y
y.description: Where the dart is, from bottom to top towards the 20: 0 is the center, 1 the outer edge of the double ring.

throw_dart.name: Enter dart
throw_dart.description: Adds a dart to the current visit as if the board had detected it, marked as entered by hand. Needs Practice manual entry. With x and y, the dart is logged where they say. Asked for a response, as by a voice assistant, it answers in words what it did or why not.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

segment.name: Bed
segment.description: Where the dart is: S1 to S20, D1 to D20, T1 to T20, 25 (or S25, SB, OB) for the outer bull, BULL (or D25, DB, 50) for the bullseye, or MISS. Needed without x and y; with them, it must be the bed at that position.

x.name: Position x
x.description: Where the dart is, from left to right: 0 is the center, 1 the outer edge of the double ring. Together with y, it gives the bed.

y.name: Position y
y.description: Where the dart is, from bottom to top towards the 20: 0 is the center, 1 the outer edge of the double ring.

player.name: Player
player.description: The name of the player the dart is for, as a voice assistant hears it. The action refuses the dart while another player is at the board.

enter_visit.name: Enter visit score
enter_visit.description: Enters an X01 visit by its score, such as 140, and passes the turn, instead of three darts. Darts already entered by hand in the visit give way to it. Needs Practice manual entry; the beds stay unknown, so only the score counts for the statistics. Asked for a response, as by a voice assistant, it answers in words what it did or why not.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

score.name: Score
score.description: The points of the visit, 0 to 180. What the player has left checks out, or busts where no visit can check it out; more busts, and so does leaving 1 with double out. Needed without checkout.

checkout.name: Checkout
checkout.description: The visit checks out what the player has left, instead of a score.

darts.name: Darts
darts.description: The darts the visit took, 1 to 3; fewer than 3 only for a checkout. Default: 3.

darts_at_double.name: Darts at a double
darts_at_double.description: How many of them were thrown at a double, for the checkout rate. Default: 1 for a checkout, otherwise 0.

player.name: Player
player.description: The name of the player the visit is for, as a voice assistant hears it. The action refuses the visit while another player is at the board.

next_player.name: Next player
next_player.description: Ends the current visit without pulling the darts, so the next player throws. Without darts, the player at the board passes in X01, the Cricket and the party games, where the pass counts as three misses. Asked for a response, as by a voice assistant, it answers in words what it did or why not.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.

undo_visit.name: Undo visit
undo_visit.description: Takes the last completed visit back: the game returns to where it was before, and the darts of the visit become the current visit again, to correct them and end the visit with Next player. The visits of the bot after it are undone, too. Asked for a response, as by a voice assistant, it answers in words what it did or why not.

config_entry_id.name: Board
config_entry_id.description: The board. Needed only with more than one board.
